request.query: Diagonal substitution of multivariate integer polynomials preserves subtraction

content.text:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "formal_name": "MvPolynomial.eval₂_sub",
      "informal_name": "Evaluation Preserves Subtraction in Multivariate Polynomials",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R) {q : MvPolynomial σ R}\n  [inst_1 : CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) (g : σ → S),\n  MvPolynomial.eval₂ f g (p - q) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ f g p - MvPolynomial.eval₂ f g q",
      "informal_description": "For any commutative ring $ R $, type $ \\sigma $, and ring $ S_1 $, and for any polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\\sigma] $, the evaluation of $ p - q $ under coefficient map $ f : R \\to S_1 $ and variable map $ g : \\sigma \\to S_1 $ satisfies $ (p - q).\\text{eval}_2(f, g) = p.\\text{eval}_2(f, g) - q.\\text{eval}_2(f, g) $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.CommRing"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.evalEval_sub",
      "informal_name": "Subtraction Commutes with Evaluation of Bivariate Polynomials",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] (x y : R) (p q : Polynomial (Polynomial R)),\n  Polynomial.evalEval x y (p - q) = Polynomial.evalEval x y p - Polynomial.evalEval x y q",
      "informal_description": "For elements $x, y$ in a semiring $R$ and bivariate polynomials $p, q \\in R[X][Y]$, the evaluation of the difference $p - q$ at $x$ and $y$ equals the difference of the evaluations of $p$ and $q$ at $x$ and $y$. Formally, $(p - q)(x, y) = p(x, y) - q(x, y)$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Bivariate"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Poly.sub_apply",
      "informal_name": "Component-Wise Subtraction of Integer Polynomials",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {α : Type u_1} (f g : Poly α) (x : α → ℕ), (f - g) x = f x - g x",
      "informal_description": "For any integer polynomials $f$ and $g$ in variables indexed by $\\alpha$, and for any exponent vector $x : \\alpha \\to \\mathbb{N}$, the value of the polynomial $f - g$ at $x$ is equal to the difference of the values of $f$ and $g$ at $x$, i.e., $(f - g)(x) = f(x) - g(x)$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.NumberTheory.Dioph"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "MvPolynomial.eval_sub",
      "informal_name": "Evaluation Preserves Subtraction in Multivariate Polynomials",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R) {q : MvPolynomial σ R} (f : σ → R),\n  (MvPolynomial.eval f) (p - q) = (MvPolynomial.eval f) p - (MvPolynomial.eval f) q",
      "informal_description": "For any commutative ring $ R $, type $ \\sigma $, and evaluation map $ f : \\sigma \\to R $, the evaluation of the difference of two multivariate polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ satisfies $ \\operatorname{eval}_f(p - q) = \\operatorname{eval}_f(p) - \\operatorname{eval}_f(q) $.",

    },

This follows from the existence of a polynomial equation with integer coefficients that encodes the relationship between the inputs and outputs of $ f $ and $ g $.",

items.informal_name: Evaluation Preserves Subtraction in Multivariate Polynomials
items.informal_description: For any commutative ring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, and ring $ S_1 $, and for any polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $, the evaluation of $ p - q $ under coefficient map $ f : R \to S_1 $ and variable map $ g : \sigma \to S_1 $ satisfies $ (p - q).\text{eval}_2(f, g) = p.\text{eval}_2(f, g) - q.\text{eval}_2(f, g) $.

items.informal_name: Subtraction Commutes with Evaluation of Bivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] (x y : R) (p q : Polynomial (Polynomial R)),
  Polynomial.evalEval x y (p - q) = Polynomial.evalEval x y p - Polynomial.evalEval x y q
items.informal_description: For elements $x, y$ in a semiring $R$ and bivariate polynomials $p, q \in R[X][Y]$, the evaluation of the difference $p - q$ at $x$ and $y$ equals the difference of the evaluations of $p$ and $q$ at $x$ and $y$. Formally, $(p - q)(x, y) = p(x, y) - q(x, y)$.

items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (f g : Poly α) (x : α → ℕ), (f - g) x = f x - g x
items.informal_description: For any integer polynomials $f$ and $g$ in variables indexed by $\alpha$, and for any exponent vector $x : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$, the value of the polynomial $f - g$ at $x$ is equal to the difference of the values of $f$ and $g$ at $x$, i.e., $(f - g)(x) = f(x) - g(x)$.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Preserves Subtraction in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R) {q : MvPolynomial σ R} (f : σ → R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval f) (p - q) = (MvPolynomial.eval f) p - (MvPolynomial.eval f) q
items.informal_description: For any commutative ring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, and evaluation map $ f : \sigma \to R $, the evaluation of the difference of two multivariate polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ satisfies $ \operatorname{eval}_f(p - q) = \operatorname{eval}_f(p) - \operatorname{eval}_f(q) $.

items.informal_name: Difference of Diophantine Functions is Diophantine
items.type: ∀ {α : Type} {f g : (α → ℕ) → ℕ}, Dioph.DiophFn f → Dioph.DiophFn g → Dioph.DiophFn fun v => f v - g v
items.informal_description: If $ f $ and $ g $ are Diophantine functions, then their difference $ f - g $ is also a Diophantine function. This follows from the existence of a polynomial equation with integer coefficients that encodes the relationship between the inputs and outputs of $ f $ and $ g $.
